comparison: Perfect agreement on C1, C36-C39. Both evaluations find ARID1A expression and localization data convincing and well-supported by single-cell RNA-seq and immunofluorescence.

Strong agreement on C2-C4, C48-C50, C53. Both find pachytene arrest well-supported by multiple assays. Peer review notes minor uncertainty about specific stage versus accumulation, but overall accepts the arrest phenotype as OpenEval does.

Agreement on C40-C42, C45-C47, C51 regarding incomplete Cre recombination. Both evaluations acknowledge this technical limitation is well-documented and appropriately addressed by authors. Peer review also includes C43-C44, C52 in same assessment.

OpenEval addresses C43-C44, C52 separately, finding the apparent contradiction resolved by incomplete Cre efficiency. Peer review groups these claims with the broader escaper cell discussion (R3), reaching the same supportive conclusion.
Perfect agreement on C54-C60. Both find RNA-seq data showing sex-linked gene upregulation convincing and well-supported, describing it as part of the MSCI defect phenotype.
Agreement on C61-C62. Both accept CUT&RUN data showing ARID1A enrichment at sex chromosomes as solid supporting evidence for MSCI role.

Agreement on C63-C67 regarding normal DDR factor localization. Both evaluations accept this finding as demonstrating ARID1A acts independently of DDR initiation. Peer review also includes C145 in their assessment and notes low resolution of ATR assessment but accepts overall conclusion.
Perfect agreement on C5, C70-C72. Both find RNAPII exclusion defect well-supported by quantitative immunofluorescence and accept this as part of the MSCI phenotype.
Perfect agreement on C6, C73-C79. Both find ATAC-seq data showing promoter accessibility changes convincing and consistent with MSCI defect.
Perfect agreement on C7, C9, C82-C86. Both find H3.3 accumulation failure at sex body well-documented by quantitative immunofluorescence and accept this as a key mechanistic finding.
Perfect agreement on C87-C89. Both accept altered H3.1/3.2 dynamics as part of the chromatin composition changes demonstrating ARID1A's role in MSCI.
Perfect agreement on C90-C93. Both accept control experiments showing normal H3.3 expression and chaperone levels, supporting direct role for ARID1A in H3.3 localization.

Strong agreement on C10, C95-C103. Both find H3.3 CUT&RUN data showing redistribution from intergenic to genic/promoter regions well-supported. Peer review also includes C108 in their assessment of this dataset.
Agreement on C104-C107. Both accept differential effects on autosomal versus sex-linked genes as part of the genome-wide H3.3 redistribution pattern demonstrating ARID1A's regulatory role.
Perfect agreement on C109-C116. Both find integrated ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN analysis convincing and accept the interpretation about H3.3 redistribution as part of a valuable dataset.

Perfect agreement on C117-C121. Both find motif enrichment and correlation with DSB markers compelling, with both noting the correlative nature of the evidence while accepting it raises interesting questions.

Agreement on C11-C12, C123-C124, C127, C149. Both find DMC1 reduction well-supported by quantitative immunofluorescence. Peer review also includes C150-C151, C157 in their assessment, describing the data as interesting and implicating ARID1A in DSB repair.

Disagreement on C125-C126, C153, C156. OpenEval finds differential DMC1/RAD51 effects supported by published SSDS data and immunofluorescence. Peer review rates this UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating only single image provided with no quantitative data, considering conclusions preliminary.

Perfect agreement on C13-C14, C128, C130-C132, C158. Both find the major conclusions about ARID1A's dual role well-supported by convergent evidence, describing the work as providing new insights with solid data supporting conclusions.

Both rate C150-C152, C157 as correlative/speculative. OpenEval explicitly marks UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct mechanistic evidence. Peer review accepts the data as 'interesting' and 'implicating' but implicitly acknowledges correlative nature by describing it as raising questions rather than answering them.

OpenEval identifies C8, C15-C35, C68-C69, C80-C81, C122, C133-C136, C139-C140, C143-C144, C154-C155 as established scientific knowledge supported by literature citations. Peer review does not separately evaluate background/context claims.

OpenEval rates C129, C137-C138, C141-C142, C145-C148 as UNCERTAIN, identifying them as speculative Discussion interpretations lacking direct experimental support. Peer review does not separately evaluate speculative mechanistic proposals, though they note C145 alongside DDR findings in R6.
